verdicts.note: Real: Stravinsky's 1925 violin-and-piano suite after Pulcinella, made with Paul Kochanski (IRCAM/Boosey & Hawkes: c. 14 min). Five movements: Introduzione, Serenata, Tarantella, Gavotta con due variazioni, Minuetto e finale (Marwood/Adès 2010 track list, 'K34, 1925 version'). It precedes and differs from the 1933 Suite italienne (6 movements, existing id 2097), so it is a separate published work; drop it only if the catalogue wants a single Pulcinella entry. Edition as drafted: Édition Russe de Musique (Berlin, (c)1926), now Boosey & Hawkes.

verdicts.title: Prélude et Ronde des princesses (from The Firebird, arr. Stravinsky)
verdicts.note: Piece is real (Firebird, violin and piano, 1929; 5:06 on BIS-2245, 4:53 Hyperion) but no source credits Kochański as ARRANGER. BIS booklet: arr. 1929 'arranged for Kochanski'; Hyperion notes: pre-Dushkin transcription made for Kochanski (1926). Wise Music (Chester/Schott, 1929) names no arranger, and it is NOT in Schott's Dushkin Transcriptions series (Berceuse = No. 31, Scherzo = No. 32). Hyperion's track list (and a Paris library record) credit 'Stravinsky & Dushkin' - chronologically doubtful (they met in 1930) but acceptable alternative: '(arr. Stravinsky & Dushkin)'. Publisher Schott / Chester (not confirmed as 'Schott 1929').

Schott ED 2294 'Pastorale - Song without words for violin and piano', transcribed by the composer and Samuel Dushkin (Dushkin Transcriptions No. 33), 1933, published 1934 (IMSLP works list K006 '3rd version'); 2:47-2:55 on BIS, Schott gives 4'. Vocalise of 1907 for Rimsky-Korsakov's daughter Nadezhda. Do not confuse with the 1933 version for violin and four winds (ED 3313).

verdicts.title: Airs du rossignol et Marche chinoise (from Le Rossignol, arr. Stravinsky & Dushkin)
verdicts.note: Exists as ONE published edition of two pieces: Boosey & Hawkes 'Airs du Rossignol & Marche Chinoise (Violin & Piano)', ISMN 9790060836589 (B&H page names no arranger; the Stravinsky & Dushkin credit comes from recording listings: Gramola 98016, Hyperion, BIS 'arr. 1932' for Dushkin). Durations: BIS-2245 5:08 + 3:07, Hyperion about 4:20 + 3:30, so minutes 6 -> 8. Title kept ('et' as in Hyperion/Strad; B&H prints '&'). Source is the opera Le Rossignol (K018), not the symphonic poem Le Chant du rossignol.

gaps.title: Scherzo (from The Firebird, arr. Stravinsky & Dushkin)
gaps.edition: Schott, Dushkin Transcriptions No. 32, ED 2250 (also in Samuel Dushkin Repertoire, Schott ED 20423, 2008)
gaps.note: Existing id 1278 'Berceuse and Scherzo' merges two separately published transcriptions; retitle 1278 to the Berceuse (see existing_issues) and add this Scherzo as its own entry. Arr. 1932 for Dushkin (BIS booklet); Dushkin/Stravinsky recorded it for Columbia in Paris, June 1933; Gringolts (BIS-2245, 2:31) and Marwood/Adès (Hyperion) also recorded it. Credit 'Stravinsky & Dushkin' as on Hyperion/Wise; Schott's series page lists no arranger.

gaps.title: Tango (arr. Dushkin)
gaps.scoring: violin and piano (Dushkin's 1941 arrangement of Stravinsky's Tango of 1940, authorised by the composer)
gaps.edition: Schott ED 9213 (arranged by Samuel Dushkin); Schott gives 4'0'', BIS recording 2:01
gaps.note: Second source: BIS-2275 booklet (Gringolts/Laul, track 21 'Tango, arranged by Samuel Dushkin') and Hyperion CDA67723 (Marwood/Adès). First played by Dushkin in New York, 3 Jan 1941; the violin version stayed unpublished for a long time, Schott edition is the current one. Not to be confused with Albéniz's Tango (also in Schott's Dushkin series, No. 14).

gaps.title: Variation d'Apollon (Apollon et les Muses) (from Apollon musagète)
gaps.scoring: violin and piano (solo-violin variation from the Apollon musagète ballet; original with strings)
gaps.edition: Boosey & Hawkes, The Stravinsky Violin Collection: 9 Pieces for Violin and Piano (ISMN 9790051106301; Hal Leonard HL 48019417)
gaps.note: Only available in the B&H collection (no stand-alone edition found; the product page credits no individual arranger, only 'arrangements made with Dushkin'). Recorded with strings on BIS-2275 (Gringolts, 3:00, 'violin and strings', B&H); whether the recorded version equals the printed piano reduction is not stated. Lower priority.

existing_issues.issue: 'Berceuse and Scherzo' combines two separate Schott transcriptions: Berceuse (ED 2186, Dushkin Transcriptions No. 31, transcribed by Stravinsky and Dushkin; 4'0'' per Schott, c. 2:47 recorded; first transcribed for Kochanski in 1929) and Scherzo (ED 2250, No. 32, arr. 1932). Suggest retitling this entry to the Berceuse and adding the Scherzo as a separate entry (see gaps). (If the owner prefers one combined entry, credit should still be 'arr. Stravinsky & Dushkin'.)
existing_issues.suggested_title: Berceuse (from The Firebird, arr. Stravinsky & Dushkin)

existing_issues.issue: Please do NOT drop: the 1944 Élégie was written for unaccompanied VIOLA (Germain Prévost, in memory of Alphonse Onnou) but is published and performed for viola or violin (violin a fifth higher, con sordino): IMSLP's Stravinsky works list K072 'va/vn' (published 1945), Schott's listing (VLB 47) 'violin or viola', Boosey & Hawkes 'Stravinsky Violin Collection' (as 'Elegie'), and Gringolts' BIS-2275 recording of the violin version. House style for works originally for another instrument: '(orig. viola)'.

House style needs the mode; IMSLP's Stravinsky works list (K053) titles it 'Violin Concerto in D major' (the composer's own title is 'Concerto en ré / in D'). Four movements Toccata, Aria I, Aria II, Capriccio, 1931.

Title order/style: Boosey & Hawkes (BH 1000297, 'Stravinsky, Igor (Dushkin)') titles it 'Chanson russe - Russian Maiden's Song' (Parasha's aria from the opera Mavra, arr. 1937). House style: original-language title first, arranger at the end.
existing_issues.suggested_title: Chanson russe (Russian Maiden's Song), from Mavra (arr. Dushkin)

existing_issues.issue: Arranger missing. The published Ballad (Boosey & Hawkes, 1951; BIS 'arr. 1947') is the violin-and-piano version proposed by the French violinist Jeanne Gautier in 1947 and approved by Stravinsky; Dushkin's earlier 'Ballad' was never approved for publication. Source work: Le Baiser de la fée (The Fairy's Kiss), 1928.
existing_issues.suggested_title: Ballad, from The Fairy's Kiss (arr. Gautier)

existing_issues.issue: Missing arranger credit and inconsistent source-work name (other entries say 'The Fairy's Kiss'). Divertimento for violin and piano was made by Stravinsky and Dushkin in 1932 (K049, published 1934, Hawkes & Son); six movements Sinfonia, Danses suisses, Scherzo, Pas de deux (Adagio, Variation, Coda); BIS-2275 timing 19:44, so minutes about 20 rather than 22.
existing_issues.suggested_title: Divertimento from The Fairy's Kiss (arr. Stravinsky & Dushkin)
